supported_short_truthful_match.source_conclusion: Structurally supported for the pinned single full-attention group with one 16-token block per chunk, provided the reported shorter count is a real contiguous, chunk-aligned host hit.
supported_short_truthful_match.lookup_state: get_num_new_matched_tokens computes a maximal hit and records num_hit_chunks/touches keys, but does not register a load job or load-token range. In this full-attention domain, the recorded hit count is not subsequently used to size the load; it only affects sliding-window touch selection, which is absent here.
supported_short_truthful_match.allocation_state: update_state_after_alloc independently uses its num_external_tokens argument to bound num_cached_tokens, slice offload_keys and destination blocks, prepare_load, and register one load job. The worker submits exactly that registered job; completion gates WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS promotion.
supported_short_truthful_match.existing_support: Natural shorter prefix hits already follow this subprefix path. No built-in capacity cap or repeated host-chunk streaming is visible. After partial completion, num_computed_tokens>0 bypasses a new connector lookup, so the remainder is locally chunk-computed when enabled.

reserve_full_isl.true: Before actual allocation, full_sequence_must_fit checks enough free blocks for min(request.num_tokens,max_model_len), including the already known preemption history. A shorter external match alone does not bypass this gate.
reserve_full_isl.false: Skips only that full-known-sequence admission check. Actual allocation still includes all returned local plus external matched tokens, optional local new work, and reserved blocks; shortening the truthful external count is independently necessary for a smaller first load.
reserve_full_isl.qualification: The current native-full adapter requires scheduler_reserve_full_isl=True; false and an intentional capacity-bounded hit have not been tested in these candidates.

limits: The maximal lookup has no capacity argument. An in-flight transfer, or a pending/retry chunk beyond a useful short prefix, can defer the whole lookup before a post-return cap can act.
The count, host keys, allocated GPU blocks, load job, completed/invalid block handling, and chunk boundaries must agree; a shorter count cannot claim unallocated or unloaded tokens as computed.

Truncation changes load versus recompute timing but cannot remove the full-attention all-history KV capacity needed by the first new output after recovery. A partial request can later self-preempt under native allocation pressure without protection.
Interface feasibility is not a performance result or a standalone recovery-admission method. The remaining experimental direction is actual recovery-admission intervention, not partial load alone.
